# Harvey

> Codebase QA for AI-generated apps — a senior quality leader in a box. (Also: AI-generated
> code review, vibe-coded app audit.) Harvey runs a ten-module audit across security, tests,
> performance, data, and maintainability, and returns one readiness verdict. It goes deepest
> on the stacks AI tools generate most: Supabase, Next.js, and Vite. Built for founders who
> shipped fast (often with AI tools like Cursor, Claude, Lovable, Bolt, or v0) and have no QA
> team.

## What Harvey is

Harvey is a productized codebase audit for AI-generated apps — an independent review of the
code your AI wrote. It is not a single-issue security scanner. It reviews the whole codebase
the way a senior quality/QA leader would and hands the founder a plain-English readiness
verdict. Security is one of ten equally weighted modules. Coverage is deepest on Supabase,
Next.js, and Vite, but the ten modules apply to any codebase. Prisma, Drizzle and other
Postgres query layers are supported alongside Supabase.

A defining principle: Harvey states what it could NOT assess. Every report carries a
coverage ledger naming each module's status and, where it could not run, the reason —
plus explicit rows for infrastructure code, source languages, and frameworks outside
what the analysis covers. An unstated limitation reads as a clean bill of health, so
nothing is silently omitted.

## The ten modules

1. Multi-tenant security — cross-tenant isolation, Row-Level Security, auth boundaries.
2. Live pen-test — a real attack on a stood-up copy of the stack (proves flaws, not flags).
3. Hotspot analysis — where code complexity and churn collide.
4. Duplication — copy-pasted logic that drifts out of sync.
5. Dead code — shipped but never run.
6. Maintainability — hand-rolled code with a better replacement.
7. Performance — N+1 queries, missing indexes, Core Web Vitals, scalability.
8. Test quality — which tests cannot actually catch a bug (mutation-tested).
9. Server-to-client boundaries — server-to-client leaks, server-action auth. Analysed on
   Next.js, Remix, React Router 7 and TanStack Start.
10. Data classification — every piece of PII/PHI/PCI, and where it lives.

## Tiers

- Free scan ($0): source-only static findings across all ten modules. No credentials.
- Connected audit (from $500, priced by codebase size): the full review with real
  verdicts plus a read of the live database (RLS, Supabase advisors, prod drift, PII).
- Full audit (from $1,000, priced by codebase size): everything in Connected plus Harvey
  stands up a copy of the stack and attacks it live, and runs full mutation testing.

Pricing scales by codebase size (small / medium / large / enterprise), measured
automatically during the free scan. Enterprise and regulated codebases are custom-quoted.

## Who it is for

Solo founders and small teams (2–5 people) running a Supabase + Next.js SaaS with real
users and no dedicated QA or security function.
